chunks: And by this chain, from Ali ibn Asbat, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

There was a piece of land to be divided between me and a man, and that man was an astrologer. He would seek the fortunate hour to go out in it, while I would go out in the inauspicious hour. So we divided, and the better of the two shares came to me. The man slapped his right hand on his left and said, "I have never seen a day like today!" I said, "Woe to another! What is that?" He said, "I am an astrologer. I made you go out in the inauspicious time and I went out in the fortunate time, then we divided and the better share came to you!"

So I said, "Shall I not narrate to you a hadith my father narrated to me?" He said, "The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever would be pleased that God repel from him the ill omen of his day, let him begin his day with charity — God will remove from him by it the ill omen of his day. And whoever loves that God remove from him the ill omen of his night, let him begin his night with charity — God will repel from him the ill omen of his night." And I said: "And I had begun my going out with charity. So this is better for you than the knowledge of astrology."

key_terms.سعود: Fortunate time, lucky stars — the astrological concept of a favorable celestial hour
key_terms.صدقة: Charity, voluntary almsgiving — a key spiritual practice in Islam with protective power
key_terms.نحوس: Ill omen, inauspiciousness — astrological concept of an unlucky celestial hour

ai.seo_question: Can charity ward off bad luck and ill omens in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates a personal account of dividing land with an astrologer who had assigned the Imam an inauspicious time, yet the Imam obtained the better share. The Imam then quoted a prophetic hadith teaching that charity at the start of one's day or night wards off any ill omen, proving Divine providence supersedes astrological timing. This account simultaneously dismisses astrology as a reliable guide for one's affairs and elevates charity as a powerful spiritual protection, grounded in a direct saying of the Prophet (SAWW).

en.hubeali:
And by this chain, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from the one who reported it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, having said, ‘

There was a piece of land between me<sup>asws</sup> and a man, and the man was an astrologer, and he used to determine the lucky time so he would go out in it, and he determined for me<sup>asws</sup> an inauspicious time to go out in. So we divided (our profits), and the better half came out for me<sup>asws</sup>. So the man struck his right hand upon the left, then said, ‘I have not seen a day like today at all!’ I said, ‘Woe be unto others, and what is that?’ He said, ‘I am an astrologer. I made you<sup>asws</sup> come out in the inauspicious time, and I went out during a lucky time. Then we divided (our profits), so the better of the two divisions came out for you<sup>asws</sup>!’.

So I<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Shall I<sup>asws</sup> narrate to you with a Hadeeth my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> narrated with? He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who is cheerful that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> should Repel from him the inauspiciousness of his day, so let him open his day with a charity. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Remove by it, from him, the inauspciousness of his day. And the one who loved that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> should Remove from him the inauspiciousness of his night, so let him open his night with charity. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Repel from him the inauscpiciousness of his night’. ‘And I<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And I<sup>asws</sup> opened my going out with a charity. So this would have been better for you than your knowledge of the stars’.
en.sarwar: 9. Through the same chain of narrators, it is narrated from Ali ibn Asbat from the chain of his narrators who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said a man and I shared a piece of land. The man was an astrologer. He would find the lucky hour for his coming out of his home and an unlucky hour for me to come out of my home. We divided it, and my share was the better one. The man struck his hand against the other and said, ‘I have never seen such a day!’ I then said, ‘Woe upon the others. What is the matter?’ He said, ‘I am an astrologer. I asked you to come out from your home in an unlucky hour, and I came out in a lucky hour. We divided it, but your share came out to be the better one.’

I then asked, ‘Can I narrate to you a Hadith my father narrated to me? The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, “If one has a wish before Allah to remove the evil of an unlucky hour from him, he should begin his day by giving charity. For giving charity, Allah removes the evil of the unlucky hour from him. If one has a wish before Allah to remove the evil of the unlucky hour of the night from him, he should begin his night by giving charity. For giving charity, Allah removes the evil of the unlucky hour of the night from him.” I began my coming out by giving charity. This is better than your astrology.’”
